verses.text: In the year that King Uzziah died I, Isaiah, saw the Lord sitting on a very high and wonderful throne. His long robe filled the Temple.
Above the Lord were Seraphims, special angels. Each angel had six wings. They used two wings to cover their faces, two wings to cover their feet, and two wings to fly.
The angels were calling to each other and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord who rules over all. His glory is everywhere on earth.
The angels talked so loudly that it caused the frame around the door to shake, and the Temple was filled with smoke.

I, Isaiah, was frightened and said: Oh, no! I will be destroyed. I am not pure enough to speak to God, and I live among people who are not pure enough to speak to God. But I have seen the King, the Lord All-Powerful.
There was a fire on the altar. One of the angels used a pair of tongs to take a hot coal from the fire. Then the angel flew to me with it in the angel's hand.
Then the angel touched my mouth with the hot coal and said: When this hot coal touched your lips, your sin was taken away, your sins were erased.
Then the Lord asked: Is there anyone who I can send? Who will take a message to the people? Then I, Isaiah, said: Here I am. Send me.
The Lord said to me: Go and tell the people: You will hear and listen to what I say, but you will not understand what I say. You will look, but you will not know what you see.
Make the heart of this people insensitive, their ears dull, and their eyes dim. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and return and be healed.

Then I, Isaiah, asked: Lord, for how long must I do this? And the Lord answered, Do this until the cities are destroyed and all the people are gone. Do this until there is no one left living in the houses and the land is destroyed and empty.
The Lord will make the people go far away, and there will be large areas of empty land in the country.

A tenth of the people will be allowed to stay in the land, but it will be destroyed again. They will be like an oak tree. When the tree is chopped down, a stump is left. This stump will be a very special seed that will grow again.

6.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs. This chapter (Isaiah's vision in the Temple) was previously mislabeled and stored under 1 Kings 6 in error; it has been moved to its correct location, Isaiah 6, and stray 'Isaiah' tags left over from the original copy/paste error have been removed.

verses.text: The LORD says: How terrible it will be for My rebellious children. They make plans, but they do not ask Me. They make agreements, but those agreements are not from My Spirit. So they add sin to sin.
They go down to Egypt without asking Me. They look to Pharaoh for strength. They hide in the shadow of Egypt for protection.
But Pharaoh's strength will bring you shame. The protection of Egypt will bring you disgrace.
Your leaders are in the city of Zoan. Your messengers have come to the city of Hanes.
Everyone will be ashamed of a people who cannot help them. That people brings no help and no good. They bring only shame and disgrace.

This is a message about the animals of the south. Your messengers travel through a land of trouble and pain. Lions and snakes and flying serpents live in that land. Your messengers carry riches on young donkeys and treasures on camels. They carry them to a people who cannot help you.
Egypt's help is worth nothing, and it does no good. So I have said about Egypt: Their strength is to sit still.
Now go. Write this on a tablet in front of them. Write it in a book. It will last for all time to come.
These people are rebellious. They are children who lie. They are children who will not listen to the LORD's teaching.
They tell the seers: Do not see. They tell the prophets: Do not tell us what is right. Tell us nice things. Tell us lies.
They say: Get out of our way. Turn away from the path. Stop talking to us about the Holy One of Israel.
So the Holy One of Israel says: You reject this message. You trust in cruelty and lies. You depend on them.
So this sin will be like a high wall with a crack in it. The wall bulges out and is ready to fall. It will break suddenly, in a moment.
The Holy One will break it like a clay pot smashed into pieces. He will not hold back. Not one piece will be big enough to carry fire from the fireplace or water from a pool.
This is what the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, says: Come back to Me and rest, and you will be saved. Be quiet and trust Me, and you will be strong. But you refused.
You said: No. We will escape on horses. So you will run away. You said: We will ride fast horses. So the ones chasing you will be fast.
One thousand of you will run away from one enemy. Five enemies will make all of you run away. Then you will be left like a lonely flagpole on top of a mountain, like a signal flag on a hill.
But the LORD is waiting to be kind to you. The LORD will rise up to show you mercy. The LORD is a God who is fair. Everyone who waits for Him is blessed.
People will live in Zion, in Jerusalem. You will not cry anymore. The LORD will be very kind when you cry for help. As soon as He hears you, He will answer you.
The Lord may give you the bread of trouble and the water of pain. But your teacher will not hide anymore. Your own eyes will see your teacher.
Your ears will hear a voice behind you saying: This is the way. Walk in it. You will hear it when you turn to the right and when you turn to the left.
You will treat your idols as unclean. Your idols are covered with silver and gold. You will throw them away like dirty rags. You will say to them: Get away from here.
Then the LORD will send rain for the seed you plant in the ground. The food from the ground will be rich and plentiful. On that day your farm animals will graze in wide fields.
The oxen and young donkeys that work the ground will eat good feed. It will be cleaned of dirt and husks with a shovel and a fork.
In the day of great killing, when the towers fall, streams of water will flow on every high mountain and every high hill.
The moon will shine like the sun. The sun will shine seven times brighter, like the light of seven days. This will happen when the LORD heals His people and bandages their wounds.
Look, the LORD comes from far away. His anger burns, and thick smoke rises. His lips are full of anger. His tongue is like a fire that burns everything up.
His breath is like a flooding river that reaches up to the neck. He will shake the nations in a sieve that destroys. He will put a bridle in the mouths of the people to lead them the wrong way.
You will sing as you do on a night of a holy feast. Your hearts will be glad, like people walking with flutes to the mountain of the LORD, to the mighty One of Israel.
The LORD will make His glorious voice heard. He will show His powerful arm coming down in anger, with flames of fire that burn everything up, with storm winds, rain, and hailstones.
The voice of the LORD will crush Assyria. Assyria hit people with a rod.
Every blow of the staff the LORD lays on Assyria will be met with tambourines and harps. The LORD will fight them with a swinging arm.

A place for burning, called Tophet, was prepared long ago. It is ready for the king. It is deep and wide. It has a pile of fire and much wood. The breath of the LORD, like a stream of burning sulfur, will set it on fire.

30.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Verses 6, 7, 28 and 32 use obscure Hebrew wording and need careful review.

verses.text: Oh, that You would tear open the sky and come down. Then the mountains would shake and flow away when You come.
It would be like fire that burns twigs, like fire that makes water boil. Then Your enemies would know Your name, and the nations would shake in fear when You come.
When You did terrible things we did not expect, You came down, and the mountains shook when You came.
From the beginning of the world, no one has heard or seen any God besides You. You act for the one who waits for You.
You meet those who gladly do what is right. You help those who remember Your ways. But You were angry, because we kept on sinning. How can we be saved?
All of us are like someone who is unclean. All our good deeds are like dirty rags. All of us dry up like a leaf. Our sins carry us away like the wind.
No one calls on Your name. No one tries to hold on to You. You have hidden Your face from us. You have let our sins destroy us.
But now, LORD, You are our Father. We are the clay, and You are the potter. All of us are the work of Your hand.
LORD, do not be so very angry. Do not remember our sins forever. Please look at us. We are all Your people.
Your holy cities have become a desert. Zion is a desert. Jerusalem is empty and destroyed.
Our holy and beautiful temple, where our fathers praised You, has been burned with fire. All the things we loved are in ruins.
LORD, will You still hold back after all this? Will You stay silent and punish us so severely?
